sources.label: CrowdStrike Falcon® Cloud Security: Cloud Detection and Response (CDR)

rows.label: Typical subscription term
rows.value: One to three years; most subscription contracts are non-cancelable

evidence.quote: subscription contracts with its customers have a typical term of one to three years and most subscription contracts are non-cancelable

rows.label: Deferred revenue treatment
rows.value: Customer advance payments are recognized as revenue over the contractual period

evidence.quote: Contract liabilities consist of deferred revenue and include payments received in advance of performance under the contract. Such amounts are recognized as revenue over the contractual period.

rows.label: Partner channel economics
rows.value: Referral fees paid to partners are capitalized when incremental to acquiring channel partner contracts

evidence.quote: The Company capitalizes referral fees paid to partners and sales commissions and associated payroll taxes paid to internal sales personnel, contractors or sales agents that are incremental to the acquisition of channel partner and direct customer contracts

blocks.title: Cloud security offering
blocks.text: CrowdStrike markets cloud detection and response for runtime cloud defense, including agent-based and agentless detection and response, cloud asset visibility, and investigation across cloud and enterprise activity.

evidence.quote: Real-time, AI-powered Cloud Detection and Response (CDR) to detect and stop active cloud attacks

blocks.title: Application described by the company
blocks.text: The offering is described as detecting and stopping active cloud attacks and helping security teams investigate incidents with cloud context.

evidence.quote: Correlate activity across cloud and the enterprise, eliminating manual triage to surface the full attack story in one place.

blocks.title: Demand and execution risks
blocks.text: The filing identifies cloud SaaS adoption, customer renewals and module additions, new-customer acquisition, competition, product efficacy, and the July 19 Incident’s continuing effects on customers, partners, reputation, results and financial condition as material risk areas.

evidence.quote: The July 19 Incident has had, and is expected to continue to have, an adverse effect on our business, sales, customer and partner relations, reputation, results of operations and financial condition.

blocks.title: Additional disclosed risks
blocks.text: The company cites long and unpredictable sales cycles and dependence on third-party and company-operated data-center facilities for hosting and operating Falcon.

evidence.quote: We rely on third-party data centers, such as Amazon Web Services, and our own colocation data centers to host and operate our Falcon platform
